technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Hyperledger Fabric v1.0 modular architecture and APIs rather than introducing a parallel application framework.
Implement peer upgrade support as a backward-compatible rolling-upgrade approach, preserving existing ledger data and defining explicit handling for protocol-version changes.
Use the current protobuf-based block and transaction structures consistently throughout ledger production code and tests.
Replace direct ledger-test dependencies on MSP security components with mocks, stubs, or narrowly scoped test fixtures.
Represent channel-creation configuration transactions with documented fields, values, serialization rules, and representative examples compatible with the channel-creation API.
Restrict chaincode invocation validation to the supported LCCC and normal application chaincode paths, rejecting unsupported system-chaincode invocations.
Implement the Node SDK using the supported Fabric client communication mechanisms, protobuf message definitions, and documented connection and transaction flows.
Use versioned documentation that clearly distinguishes stable v0.6 operational guidance from in-development v1.0 guidance.
Provide architecture diagrams and executable or demonstrable scripts for the principal v1.0 transaction and network flows.
Add unit, integration, compatibility, and regression tests for all modified ledger, upgrade, validation, documentation examples, and SDK behavior.
assumptions: The estimate covers one software increment implementing all eight user stories and includes development, tests, documentation, examples, and release preparation.
The existing Fabric repository, build system, protobuf definitions, peer components, ledger implementation, and test infrastructure are available and buildable.
No new consensus algorithm, membership service, storage engine, or deployment platform is required.
Peer upgrades must preserve ledger contents and support compatibility with existing data formats; a complete automated migration framework for arbitrary future protocol changes is out of scope.
The channel-creation API referenced by FAB-687 and any related upstream change can be reused or adapted rather than implemented as an entirely new API.

The Node SDK is an initial usable SDK, not a complete production replacement for every Fabric client feature; it covers network connection, channel interaction, chaincode invocation, query, event handling, and transaction submission needed by representative applications.

Documentation and visual aids are delivered as repository-maintained Markdown or equivalent pages, diagrams, and scripts; professional graphic design, localization, and hosted website operations are out of scope.
Security review is limited to implementation-level checks and automated tests; an independent formal security audit is not included.
Workdays represent focused effort by one developer and include normal coding, debugging, test execution, and local review effort, but not elapsed calendar time or external stakeholder waiting time.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing peer, ledger, chaincode, API, SDK, documentation, and test code; map each user story to affected components; define acceptance criteria and an implementation sequence.

Improve the new-visitor entry points, quick-start guidance, information structure, links, and basic examples so users can quickly identify installation, first-run, development, and operational resources.

Analyze the channel-creation transaction format, document fields and valid values, provide serialized and human-readable examples, align the description with the channel API and related upstream work, and add validation examples.

activities.activity_name: Peer protocol upgrade and data-preservation support
activities.activity_description: Design and implement peer version compatibility checks, upgrade handling, startup or migration safeguards, and regression coverage demonstrating that existing ledger data remains usable across supported protocol changes.

Find remaining production and test code using obsolete block structures, update construction and parsing to the current structures, remove stale compatibility assumptions, and repair affected ledger unit and integration tests.
Refactor ledger unit tests to use isolated mocks or fixtures instead of explicit MSP security dependencies, while retaining meaningful authorization and identity-related coverage where required.
Prepare v1.0 architecture diagrams, component and transaction-flow explanations, and runnable demonstration scripts showing representative network, channel, ledger, and chaincode behavior.
Create or update documentation that directs users seeking a stable operational platform to v0.6 and provides current v1.0 installation, development, API, operational, and limitation guidance.

Implement validation that accepts only LCCC or supported normal chaincode invocation targets, rejects unsupported system-chaincode or malformed requests, and adds unit and integration tests for accepted and rejected cases.

Implement the Node SDK package structure, connection and enrollment configuration, channel and peer interaction, chaincode query and invoke operations, transaction submission, event handling, error mapping, examples, and API documentation.

Run and extend end-to-end tests covering channel creation, peer upgrade behavior, ledger compatibility, chaincode validation, Node SDK workflows, and representative documentation scripts; diagnose and fix integration defects.

Update build and dependency metadata, package the Node SDK and examples, verify reproducible test and demonstration commands, prepare change notes, and perform final cleanup and review of the increment.
